topic.name: The Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Differentiation

question.explanation:
The function $f(x)$ is the sum of three power functions. So, we apply the sum rule, and we get

\[ \begin{align} f'(x) & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x^3 + \dfrac{1}{x^2} - x\right) \\[2pt] & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x^3\right) + \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x^{-2}\right) - \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x\right) \\[2pt] & = 3x^{(3-1)} + (-2)x^{(-2-1)} - 1 \\[2pt] & = 3x^2 - 2x^{-3} - 1 \\ & = 3x^2 - \dfrac{2}{x^3} - 1. \end{align} \]

example.title: Differentiating a Sum of Functions Without Constant Factors Using the Sum Rule

question.explanation:
Here, we apply the addition, constant multiple, and power rules:

\[ \begin{align} \dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(5x^{15} - 4x^8 + 7x^5\right) \\[2pt] & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(5x^{15}\right) - \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(4x^8\right) + \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(7x^5\right) \\[2pt] & = 5\cdot \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x^{15}\right) - 4\cdot \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x^8\right) + 7\cdot \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x^5\right) \\[2pt] & = 5 \cdot 15x^{(15-1)} - 4\cdot 8x^{(8-1)} + 7\cdot 5x^{(5-1)} \\[2pt] & = 75x^{14} - 32x^7 + 35x^4 \end{align} \]

example.title: Differentiating a Sum of Functions With Constant Factors

question.explanation:
Here, we apply the addition, constant multiple, and power rules:

\[ \begin{align} \dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x} &= \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(3x^4 +\dfrac{4}{x^3} + 12\right) \\[2pt] & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(3x^{4}\right) +\dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(4x^{-3}\right) + \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(12\right) \\[2pt] & = 3\cdot \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x^{4}\right) + 4\cdot \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x^{-3}\right) + \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(12\right) \\[2pt] & = 3 \cdot 4x^{(4 - 1)} + 4\cdot (-3)x^{(-3-1)} + 0 \\[2pt] & = 12x^3 - 12x^{-4} \\[2pt] & = 12x^3 - \dfrac{12}{x^4} \end{align} \]

example.title: Differentiating a Sum of Functions With Constant Factors

question.explanation:
We first rewrite the function as

\[ y = -\dfrac{5}{x^7} = -5x^{-7}. \]

Then, we apply the constant multiple and power rules:

\[ \begin{align} \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x}&= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( -5x^{-7} \right) \\[2pt] &= -5\cdot \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( x^{-7} \right) \\[2pt] &= -5 \cdot (-7)x^{-7-1} \\[2pt] &= 35x^{-8} \\[2pt] &=\dfrac{35}{x^{8}}. \end{align} \]
